items.text: a constant vus and duration profile offered as the ramped test
items.reason: The Load Profiles table gives the constant profile as vus/duration and a separate ramp-up stress profile with staged targets, so the constant shape is never offered as the ramped test.
The document provides a dedicated spike test with a 50→500→50 stage shape plus recovery window.

items.text: no scoped threshold for recovery window
items.reason: The spike recipe scopes thresholds to the recovery window via 'http_req_duration{phase:recovery}' and requires it in Done When.
All k6 thresholds and Lighthouse assertions carry explicit numeric limits (p(95)<500, maxNumericValue: 2500, etc.).
The Playwright CWV recipe includes setTimeout fallbacks (resolve(-1) after 10000ms, resolve(score) after 3000ms) rather than a bare hardcoded wait.

items.text: single scenario instead of three concurrent
items.reason: The scenarios recipe models three concurrent flows (browse, checkout, api_heavy) running at once.
The scenarios example uses per-scenario thresholds tagged with {scenario:browse} and {scenario:checkout}.
Exit code 97 is explicitly called out in the migration callout and the CI section as something to handle.
The document repeatedly warns against optimizing without profiling and lists it as an anti-pattern.

items.text: client-side metrics only without server context
items.reason: Ignoring server-side metrics is listed as an anti-pattern and bottleneck step 5 requires correlating with server metrics.
k6 scripts drive BASE_URL from __ENV with only a localhost fallback; the document explicitly instructs driving the base URL from __ENV.

items.text: no failure condition on threshold breach
items.reason: The document states k6 exits non-zero on any threshold breach and that Lighthouse error assertions fail the build.
The document carefully distinguishes field vs. lab data, including a comparison table and the INP-is-field-only section.
